summary.headline: Pearl Global H1 FY27 revenue rose 31.1% to INR3,330 crores with adjusted EBITDA margin of 10.5% and PAT of INR225 crores.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue reached a record INR1,802 crores (up 37.2% YoY), with adjusted EBITDA of INR184 crores (10.2% margin) and PAT of INR126 crores (up 74.7%). Growth was driven by shipment volumes (43.6 million pieces in H1 vs 37.1 million in H1 FY26) and FTA-related sourcing interest from UK and EU customers. Working capital days rose to 56 from receivable days moving from 30 to 50, due to late-quarter shipments and deferred factoring; management expects normalisation over the next two quarters. Management flagged a Bangladesh minimum wage revision expected in December, with an unresolved wage figure.

segments.name: United States
segments.commentary: Largest market at roughly half of group revenue; retailers entered peak season with lean inventory and Thanksgiving falls on 26 Nov, compressing the selling window by about 12-12.5%.

segments.name: UK and Canada
segments.commentary: Management cited strong growth in Canada and UK this year; India-UK FTA effective 15 July 2026 is driving a significant rise in UK volumes.

segments.name: European Union
segments.commentary: Volumes inching up; EU FTA expected to take effect by early 2027 with elevated customer interest.

segments.name: Bangladesh
segments.commentary: New 7 million pieces p.a. unit inaugurated in Q2 (about 20% operational); 10 tonnes knitting phase started; INR350-375 crore knitting and processing backward integration project to be operational by early 2028; CWIP INR225 crore expected to be capitalised in Q3-Q4 FY27.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation about 68-69% in H1; Bihar plant ramping up with hiring and training; Haryana wage and PF increases affect four Haryana factories.

segments.name: Vietnam and Indonesia
segments.commentary: Vietnam growing steadily, with capex under evaluation after land acquisition completed; Indonesia growing from a much lower base. Both are driving realisation improvement.

segments.name: Guatemala
segments.commentary: Management is working to stabilise operations and reach breakeven; no figures given.

guidance_outlook: Revenue of INR6,000 crores-plus expected in FY27 (earlier target: by FY28); management said it is confident of reaching this within the year, on value terms.
EBITDA margin trajectory of 12-14% over the next four years (roadmap from September 2026 Investor Day), with progress shown in H1.
Working capital and receivable days expected to normalise in Q3 and Q4 FY27, improving free cash flow in H2 FY27.
Blended tax rate of about 15% considered appropriate on a long-term basis.
Management is not forecasting further net tariff gains; any future benefit may come as partnership gains rather than refunds.
Capex: INR900-950 crore capitalisation over FY27-FY30, with the full amount expected to be capitalised by FY29 per management.
capex_capacity: CWIP of INR225 crores at 30 Sep 2026, mainly Bangladesh, expected to be capitalised in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Capacity expansion capex of INR325-350 crores across geographies; INR100 crores to be capitalised in FY27 and remainder under evaluation, including Vietnam and Indonesia (about INR225-250 crores).

Backward integration (knitting and processing) in Bangladesh: INR350-375 crores capex, INR200 crores approved by board; operational by beginning of 2028; commitment expected to start this fiscal year.
Bihar plant ramping up; India utilisation about 68-69% in H1, expected to rise by year-end.
New Bangladesh 7 million piece unit: about 20% operational, full capacity expected in 6-8 months.
demand_pricing: US retailers kept inventories lean into peak season; management sees no major change in inventory planning but expects a shift between national brands and private label.
Shipping container spot rates peaked at about USD 12,500 per container versus a normal USD 2,000-3,000; retailers are locking long-term contracts.
ASPs reportedly up about 15-20% YoY; management attributed part of realisation gain to a 7-8% INR depreciation (partly offset on cost side) and product mix (knits vs woven).
Knits were about 31% of H1 revenue per management's split referenced by an analyst.
Turkey and China seen losing sourcing share to India, Vietnam and Bangladesh; management expects fungibility between Bangladesh and India to support volumes.
Management said the growth was partly a rebound from a suppressed FY26 (growth below 9%) and that 30%+ growth is unlikely to be sustained next year.

qa_highlights.question: Are US brands restocking given tariffs have eased, and what is the sense from customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retailers remain cautious with lean inventories ahead of a compressed holiday season; the mix is shifting between national brands and private label, and consumer demand has not shown a major change.

qa_highlights.question: What wage increase is expected in Bangladesh and how will margins be affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the wage to rise to roughly 15,000-18,000 taka from about 13,000 taka; it views a 15%-plus increase as its working assumption, says the cost is partly included in Q3-Q4 costing, and expects taka depreciation and productivity to offset part of the impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value-added services margin and will it be part of guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said VAS revenue was INR98 crores at about 1.5% EBITDA margin, is a customer-retention tool not included in forecasts, and removing it leaves the margin roughly unchanged; the INR6,000 crore guidance is said to include it.

qa_highlights.question: Is the net tariff gain recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 included about INR10 crores of net tariff adjustment from partnership discussions with customers; management is not forecasting it and says it may come as partnership business rather than refunds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin driver and gross margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the 12-14% EBITDA margin path, driven by pricing, cost improvement and operating leverage; it advised tracking EBITDA rather than gross margin because outsourcing costs can sit in other expense lines.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR6,000 crore FY27 target imply a sharp H2 slowdown, and what is the capex breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q3 order book is healthy, Q4 orders will build over the coming weeks, and there is no slowdown; capex is INR900-950 crores through FY30, with CWIP of INR225 crores as part of that, the same INR675-725 crore growth capex in the presentation.

risks_watch: Bangladesh wage board outcome in early December (management's expected range 15,000-18,000 taka vs about 13,000 taka) and arrears due in January; analyst estimate of 3-3.5% margin hit if the wage rises about 40%.
Political unrest in Dhaka: plants were halted when mobs approached, about two days lost across three factories; all five own factories were fully running as of the call.
Working capital: receivable days at 50 (from 30) and short-term borrowing up INR210 crores; normalisation in Q3-Q4 depends on factoring and collections.
Haryana wage hike and PF changes; Karnataka wage pressure exempted for garments for now.
US holiday season compression and potential slowdown in H2; management says it sees no slowdown yet.
FY27 revenue guidance of INR6,000 crores+ implies sharp H2 deceleration from H1 growth of 31%; volume guidance not given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, FTA tailwinds and margin trajectory, but cautious on Bangladesh wage risk and working capital; management answered most questions with ranges and avoided firm forward numbers on volume and wage outcomes.
key_quotes: We are one of those few established company who can serve them from both the countries.
Both these will get normalized within this year itself, within this next two quarters.
So we don't see, as of now, unless we'll see how the impact comes up.

adds.what: New Bangladesh 7 million pieces p.a. unit (about 20% operational)
Bangladesh knitting and processing backward integration project (10 tonnes knitting phase started; full project operational by early 2028)
Bangladesh CWIP INR225 crore expected to be capitalised in Q3-Q4 FY27
Capacity expansion capex INR100 crore to be capitalised in FY27; Vietnam/Indonesia (INR225-250 crore) under evaluation

growth.why: Management reiterates confidence in FY27 revenue of INR6,000 crore-plus (value terms, raised from earlier FY28 target), backed partly by Bangladesh capacity (new 7 mn pcs unit ~20% operational, INR225 crore CWIP to capitalise Q3-Q4 FY27) and FTA-driven UK demand, but management also says 30%+ growth is unlikely to be sustained next year and no specific order book numbers were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Adjusted EBITDA margin rose 120 bps to 10.5% in H1 and 90 bps to 10.2% in Q2, with management working toward a 12-14% four-year path, but Bangladesh wage hike (15%+ working assumption, partly in Q3-Q4 costing) and loss of ~INR10 crore one-time tariff gain are headwinds.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: INR225 crore Bangladesh CWIP to be capitalised in Q3-Q4 FY27, the new 7 mn pcs unit is about 20% operational with full capacity in 6-8 months, and the INR350-375 crore knitting project is due by early 2028.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 shipments rose to 43.6 mn pieces from 37.1 mn (about 17.5%), with Q3 order book described as healthy, UK volumes lifting on India-UK FTA effective 15 July 2026, and India utilisation at 68-69% with room to rise, though management says 30%+ growth is unlikely next year.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 68-69% in India so a fresh India plant is not needed, but INR225-250 crore for Vietnam/Indonesia is under evaluation after land acquisition and remaining capex of INR325-350 crore is not yet fully committed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue target was already raised to INR6,000 crore-plus, implying H2 revenue of about INR2,670 crore versus H1 INR3,330 crore, which the company frames as achievable with healthy Q3 order book; further raise depends on US peak season and FTA ramp.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Bangladesh wage hike of about 15%+ (analyst estimates 3-3.5% margin hit at ~40% rise), US Thanksgiving compression of 12-12.5% in selling window, and receivable days at 50 versus 30 create risk to H2 margins and cash flow.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or model launches were discussed; growth is capacity and FTA-led rather than new-product-led.

rows.label: Receivable days normalise from 50 to 30-ish
rows.why: Management expects working capital and receivable days (56 days, receivables up from 30 to 50) to normalise in Q3 and Q4 FY27, improving H2 free cash flow, though short-term borrowing rose INR210 crore and depends on factoring and collections.

rows.label: EU FTA effect on sourcing
rows.why: EU FTA expected to take effect by early 2027 with elevated customer interest, but EU volumes are only inching up today.

rows.label: Bangladesh minimum wage revision
rows.why: Wage board outcome expected early December with arrears due January; management working assumption is 15%+ increase from about 13,000 to 15,000-18,000 taka, partly costed in Q3-Q4.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 INR6,000 crore-plus revenue, FTA demand and the margin path, but cautious on the Bangladesh wage hike, working capital and US holiday compression; analysts pressed on H2 deceleration implied by guidance, tariff gain recurrence and capex breakup.
